newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZOG to farm out 50 pct of NZ licence.
newsitem.headline: NZOG to farm out 50 pct of NZ licence.

text.p: New Zealand Oil and Gas said on Friday it had invited a range of local and international oil and gas companies to bid for 50 percent equity in its PEP-38460 exploration licence, situated west of the Maui gas field offshore from the west coast of the North Island.
NZOG finance manager Gordon Ward said the company hoped to secure funds for the drilling of at least one well by farming out the 50 percent equity interest.

"The intention is to farm out half the equity in the licence in order to get free carry through the drilling of at least one well, and we're hoping that there will be more than one well borne by the party," he told Reuters.
He said drilling costs for one well were usually in the vicinity of NZ$10-12 million.
"If we can farm it out, then it's worth to us I guess what the cost saving is on the drilling of the well.
"If you've got $12 million in drilling costs, they'd be paying $6 million for a 50 percent equity," he said, but added that in the end, the price could be a lot higher or a lot lower.
"We're hopeful that we'll get more than one well built on this particular acreage, and it's not worth a great deal until you've actually got somebody to sign up.
"We see very exciting potential in the prospect...but until we actually get somebody to come in an drill the well, it doesn't have a lot of value."
Seismic data showed the licence had exciting potential.
Tui, a large stratigraphic propsect extending over 300 square kilometres, had the potential to recover as much as 500 million barrels of condensate in the event of a discovery.
Tahuroa, a dome shaped structure extending more than 80 square kilometres, was of a size to contain up to 400 million barrels of recoverable oil.
And Hector, a large stratigraphic prospect with 100 square kilometres within the block, had potential in the order of up to 500 million barrels of recoverable oil.
Several other less well defined or smaller features had also been recognised and may develop to drillable status.
If the farm-out proceeded as planned, drilling would be expected to commence around mid-1998, subject to rig availability.
